title: feat(spec,plugin-audit): publish the sys_activity.type built-in vocabulary from @objectstack/spec (#11807)
body:
Fixes #11807

## What

`sys_activity.type`'s built-in vocabulary existed only inside `plugin-audit`'s object declaration, so UI packages hand-copied it — and the copy drifted the same day #11522 declared `scheduled`. This PR publishes the set where consumers can read it:

- **`packages/spec/src/data/feed.zod.ts`** — new exports `SYS_ACTIVITY_BUILTIN_TYPES` (a plain `as const` tuple) and `SysActivityBuiltinType` (derived union), co-located with `FeedItemType` as the issue proposed. The TSDoc states the #11507 boundary: this is the **built-in set of an OPEN, author-extensible vocabulary, never the column's value domain** — consumers must render unknown values, not drop or reject them. It is deliberately **not** a `z.enum`: a Zod schema here would read as a validator and quietly re-close the vocabulary.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts`** — the `type` field's options now spread the published constant instead of inlining the list (single source; parsed output is byte-identical, so the generated i18n bundles do not move).
- **`sys-activity-type-vocabulary.test.ts`** — new wiring pin: the object's declared options must equal the published set, so a diverging re-inlined list cannot come back silently. The existing literal writer census is kept verbatim and now transitively pins the spec constant: editing the published set without redoing the census goes red there. Chain closed in both directions: spec constant === object declaration === writer census.
- **`packages/spec/src/data/feed.test.ts`** — mechanical invariants for the new export (non-empty, unique, snake_case; plain tuple with no `parse`/`safeParse` affordance). The semantic census deliberately stays in plugin-audit — a second literal inventory in spec would be a second copy that can drift, which is what this card retires.
- Regenerated (via `check:generated --fix`, only the four proved stale): `api-surface/data.json`, `export-origins/data.json`, `content/docs/references/data/feed.mdx`, `skills/objectstack-ui/references/_index.md`.
- Changeset: `@objectstack/spec` **minor** (new public export), `@objectstack/plugin-audit` **patch**. Additive — no ADR-0087 disposition required (`check:adr-0087-registration` green).

Out of scope, unchanged here: objectui's census pin retires in the UI lane after the pin bump (objectui#5969 lineage; cross-repo mirror gap already tracked as #8852). #11507 remains the governing ruling — nothing here narrows `activityMilestones[].type` or adds enforcement, and #11522 stays untouched by this PR.

## App-side extension interaction — measured, two-layer shape NOT needed

The #11807 dispatch asked whether the published set must be two-layer ("built-in + extensions"). Measured answer: **no.**

1. Extension values are app-owned and runtime-only. The sanctioned channel `activityMilestones[].type` is `z.string().optional()` (`object.zod.ts:2021`) forwarded verbatim by `audit-writers.ts:1328` (`if (milestone.type) activityType = milestone.type`); app actions insert directly (both measured sites live in hotcrm, per the census). Spec cannot enumerate those at build time — a published "extension layer" would be structurally empty or a lie.
2. No consumer needs the union. In-repo, the only enumerators of the vocabulary are the object declaration (now derived) and the census test. The cross-repo consumer (objectui `recordActivityFeed.ts`) is an open map — `ACTIVITY_TYPE_TO_FEED_TYPE`, a readonly record keyed by arbitrary string whose values are optional FeedItemType entries (the angle-bracket generic is spelled in words here because the platform body sanitizer eats it) — with `UNMAPPED_ACTIVITY_FEED_TYPE = 'system'` fallback plus a one-shot diagnostic, so app-contributed values already render generically with no published list required.
3. The single layer handles adoption. An app value colliding with a built-in name simply is that built-in; promoting an app value into the platform set is a deliberate spec edit + census redo (the `scheduled`/#11522 precedent), which one layer expresses as an ordinary addition.

## Governed surface note (generated, zero net growth)

`gen:skill-refs` synced one module-description line in `skills/objectstack-ui/references/_index.md` (the feed.zod.ts header line). Readings: changed file **56 → 56 lines**; whole published catalog SKILL.md sum **10512 → 10512 lines** (net 0). No hand edits to `skills/**`. Because the diff touches `skills/**`, this PR is **human-merge only** (Prime Directive #14) — do not queue, arm, or flip it out of draft.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` — VERDICT `command-exit 0`; `check-dts-emitted: @objectstack/spec - 34/34 declared declaration file(s) present.`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — re-run at this head after the reverse-verification rebuild: "All 14 generated artifacts are up to date." (verbatim); api-surface delta is exactly `+ SYS_ACTIVITY_BUILTIN_TYPES (const)`, `+ SysActivityBuiltinType (type)`, no removals.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — `Test Files  428 passed (428)`, `Tests  11403 passed (11403)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK`).
- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-audit^...' build` — VERDICT `command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit test` — `Test Files  22 passed (22)`, `Tests  326 passed (326)`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit typecheck` — exit 0.
- Gate battery (dispatch list ∪ `dispatch-gates.mjs` re-derivation on the actual diff): 50 gates green, listed in the dev report. `check:dev-prereqs` red is a fresh-worktree precondition (52/67 workspace packages unbuilt — none of them touched here; spec dist freshly built and hash-stamped), not a finding of this diff; CI builds the workspace before running it.
- Reverse verification (single-source drift tripwire): adding a probe value to `SYS_ACTIVITY_BUILTIN_TYPES` turns the census set-equality test red while the wiring pin stays green (object follows spec); restoring turns everything green. plugin-audit's vitest aliases `@objectstack/spec/*` to source (`vitest.config.ts`), so no rebuild is involved in either leg; the mutation and its restoration were both confirmed on disk by grep before each run.
